title: What Portfolio Should You Look For in a Westchester Architect
excerpt: Choosing an architect for your Westchester home is about more than just seeing pretty pictures. Here's what actually matters when you're reviewing a portfolio.
content:
When you're looking to hire an architect for a home renovation, addition, or new build in Westchester, you're going to see portfolios. Lots of them. Some will be slick. Some will be overwhelming. The question is: what are you actually supposed to be looking at?

A strong portfolio doesn't just show you what an architect thinks looks good. It shows you what they can actually deliver in your neighborhood, with your constraints, and within the reality of how Westchester construction actually works.

Look for Work in Your Town and Similar Communities

This matters more than you might think. A licensed architect in Westchester, NY who has completed work in Scarsdale, Bronxville, or Larchmont understands the architectural character of those areas. They know what the neighborhoods expect. They know how those towns review plans.

That said, experience matters across the whole county. A residential architect in Scarsdale might do excellent work in Mamaroneck or Rye because the same principles apply. You're looking for someone who has navigated permit processes in multiple municipalities and knows how to work within those frameworks.

If most of a portfolio is from one town or one region entirely outside Westchester, ask why. You want someone who knows the area where your home sits.

Check if They Actually Show the Before and After

This is simple but revealing. A good portfolio shows what a space looked like and what it became. Kitchen renovations, bathroom updates, second-story additions, open-concept conversions. All of these can be done well or done poorly.

When you look at before and afters, ask yourself: Does the new work fit the house? Does it look like someone thought about how the addition or renovation connects to what was already there? Or does it look like it was just bolted on?

Projects in towns like Harrison, Pelham, and White Plains often show how an architect handles different house styles and lot sizes. If someone's portfolio includes work across that range, they've had to solve real problems, not just copy one solution over and over.

Verify They Do Design-Build Work if That's What You Need

Not every architect is also a general contractor. Some are one or the other. When you're looking at a portfolio from a design-build firm in Westchester, you should see projects where one person or team handled both the architectural design and the actual construction.

Why does this matter? Because when your architect is also your contractor, there's accountability from start to finish. There's no finger-pointing between two different companies about who caused a problem. The person who designed it is the person building it.

This model works especially well for home additions in Westchester, historic restorations in towns like Hastings-on-Hudson or Tarrytown, and custom homes where the design and construction need to move in sync.

Make Sure the Portfolio Matches Your Project Type

If you need a custom home in Westchester County, you want to see custom homes in the portfolio. If you're doing a primary suite addition, look for primary suite additions. This is straightforward, but a lot of homeowners skip it.

The skills needed for a kitchen remodel are different from the skills needed for a second-story addition. Both are valuable. Neither makes someone good at the other automatically. A solid portfolio will show depth in the type of work you're actually planning to do.
